source.title: Properly Coloured Cycles and Paths: Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For each fixed integer c ≥ 2, determine whether there exists a constant s(c) depending only on c such that, as n grows, the minimum integer d(n,c) with the property that every c-edge-coloured graph on n vertices and minimum monochromatic degree at least d(n,c) contains a properly coloured cycle satisfies d(n,c) = s(c) log_2 n (1 + o(1)).
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotic threshold for properly coloured cycles

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2. [15] There is a function s(c) dependent only on c such that d(n, c) = s(c) log2 n(1 + o(1)).

accepted.question_text: Determine the specific constant s(2) in the asymptotic formula d(n,2) = s(2) log_2 n (1 + o(1)), where d(n,2) is the minimum integer k such that every 2-edge-coloured graph on n vertices and minimum monochromatic degree at least k contains a properly coloured cycle.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2. [15] There is a function s(c) dependent only on c such that d(n, c) = s(c) log2 n(1 + o(1)).
In particular, it would be interesting to determine s(2).

accepted.question_text: Among all graph gadgets G_x associated with a vertex x and its incident colour set χ(x), where G_x must satisfy properties P1-P4 so that it can serve as a P-gadget in the authors' reduction from properly coloured subgraph problems to perfect matching problems, determine whether the XP-gadget always has the minimum possible numbers of vertices and edges for every value z = |χ(x)| ≥ 2.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1. The XP-gadget has the minimum number of vertices and edges among all possible P-gadgets for every z ≥ 2.

accepted.question_text: For the transformation method that converts an edge-coloured multigraph into an ordinary graph so that properly coloured cycle and properly coloured (s,t)-path problems can be solved via perfect matchings, determine an optimal transformation that minimizes the order and size of the transformed graph while preserving the needed correspondence with properly coloured subgraphs.

evidence.quote: We raise a problem of finding the optimal transformation and consider a possible solution to the problem.
We raise a problem of determining the minimum order and size of the transformed graph, and describe the family of graphs that may be the solution to the problem.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a c-edge-coloured multigraph on n vertices. If the minimum monochromatic degree satisfies δ_mon(G) ≥ ceil(n/2), must G always contain a Hamilton properly coloured cycle when c ≥ 3, and when c = 2 with n even, and a properly coloured cycle of length n - 1 when c = 2 with n odd?
accepted.context_brief: Weakened degree condition for long properly coloured cycles

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.2. [1] Theorem 5.1 holds if we replace δmon(G) ≥ ⌈n+1/2⌉ by δmon(G) ≥ ⌈n/2⌉.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a c-edge-coloured graph of order n with minimum monochromatic degree d = δ_mon(G) ≥ 1. Must G always contain a properly coloured path of length at least min{n - 1, 2cd}?
accepted.context_brief: Lower bound for properly coloured paths in graphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.4. Let G be a c-edge-coloured graph of order n and let d = δmon(G) ≥ 1. Then G has a PC path of length at least min{n − 1, 2cd}.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a c-edge-coloured multigraph of order n with minimum monochromatic degree d = δ_mon(G) ≥ 1. Must G always contain a properly coloured path of length at least min{n - 1, 2d}?
accepted.context_brief: Lower bound for properly coloured paths in multigraphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.5. Let G be a c-edge-coloured multigraph of order n with δmon(G) = d ≥ 1. Then G has a PC path of length at least min{n − 1, 2d}.

accepted.question_text: For c ≥ 3, determine the computational complexity of deciding whether a c-edge-coloured complete graph K_n^c contains a properly coloured Hamilton cycle.
accepted.context_brief: Complexity of properly coloured Hamilton cycle problem

evidence.quote: Problem 6.4 Determine the complexity of the PC Hamilton cycle problem for c-edge-coloured complete graphs when c ≥ 3.

accepted.question_text: For a fixed number of colours c ≥ 3, find a characterization of those c-edge-coloured complete graphs K_n^c that contain a properly coloured Hamilton cycle.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of complete graphs with properly coloured Hamilton cycles

evidence.quote: In fact, no characterization of Kc_n with a PC Hamilton cycle is known for any fixed c ≥ 3 and it is a very interesting problem to obtain such a characterization.

accepted.question_text: For c ≥ 3, determine whether the properly coloured Hamilton cycle problem on c-edge-coloured complete graphs is polynomial-time solvable.

evidence.quote: We conjecture that the PC Hamilton cycle problem for c-edge-coloured complete graphs when c ≥ 3 is polynomial-time solvable.

accepted.question_text: Does every c-edge-coloured complete graph K_n^c with maximum monochromatic degree Δ_mon(K_n^c) ≤ floor(n/2) - 1 necessarily contain a properly coloured Hamilton cycle?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.6. Every Kc_n with Δmon(Kc_n) ≤ ⌊n/2⌋ − 1 has a PC Hamilton cycle.

accepted.question_text: For c ≥ 3, determine how to find a longest properly coloured cycle in a c-edge-coloured complete graph K_n^c, or equivalently resolve the still-unsolved longest properly coloured cycle problem in this setting.
accepted.context_brief: Longest properly coloured cycle in complete graphs

evidence.quote: The problem of finding a longest PC cycle Kc_n has not been solved yet for c ≥ 3 as we will see below.
